analysis.title: GS Armbrust - What Matters Today: US Equity Outlook, Three US Consumer Themes, CTA + Vol Control + Risk Parity Positioning (17 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Goldman forecasts the S&P 500 at 8,700 by year-end, a 17% rise, versus a 21% annualized return over the past four years.
EPS growth is expected to slow from roughly 30% in 2026 to 18% in 2027. The base case holds the P/E near its current 18x because of elevated interest rates and AI uncertainty.

AI trade theme: decelerating AI capex growth suggests the trade shifts from AI infrastructure stocks to monetization and adoption beneficiaries, including hyperscalers. GS favors AI productivity candidates with physically-intensive business models that reduce disruption risk (Exhibit 50).
Re-leveraging theme: AI spending has raised leverage and weighed on buyback growth in parts of the market. GS expects 'buyback aristocrats' with strong free cash flow to outperform (Exhibit 51).

Growth factor: decelerating S&P 500 earnings favor secular growth, accelerating earnings and upward revisions, and valuation dispersion is tight. Energy infrastructure shows rare 2027 earnings acceleration, and Transports offer cyclical exposure for a macro upside scenario.
Diversification theme: Health Care and parts of Consumer Staples trade at discounted valuations to trend earnings. Mid-caps trade at discounted valuations and are not over-earning.
XLP hit another all-time high on 11/16, up 10% over the last month and 21% YTD. GS describes it as largely one momentum trade, with better 3Q HPC and Beauty earnings a secondary factor.

GS PB flows in Staples: the desk was buying a month ago but has been better for sale for the last 2 weeks, led almost entirely by shorts. Last week was 6-1 better for sale across Staples sub-sectors. Investors are fighting the move, not embracing it.

Retail earnings: GS expects more beats than misses over the next 2 weeks. HD and AS beats on 11/17 were expected, and both raised the sales guide. Strong results are expected from TGT, LOW, WMT, WSM, ROST and BJ.
TJX is seen as the hardest retail print this week for client sentiment, since investor feedback says the quarter was choppy. Upside is expected next week at BBY, KSS and ANF.
Discretionary was one of only three sub-sectors bought last week. November is historically the best month for Retail, with most of the 10-year outperformance in the last 2 weeks of the month.

HD and LOW have held up despite high-profile sell-side downgrades from other firms and a very tough housing environment. GS lists possible reasons: expectations of the HD beat, optimism on housing policy relief (which GS doubts), or positioning.

CTAs sold over $22bn of S&P in the past week and almost $2.5bn of Nasdaq, with Russell roughly flat. Net US equity positioning is short almost $10bn, the lowest since April, and flows are skewed asymmetrically to the upside for the first time in weeks.

GS models estimate vol control and risk parity sold over $30bn combined last week. After the CPI print, stocks and bonds fell together, which typically leads risk parity to cut exposure, though GS does not expect the selling to be dramatic.
Vol control may re-risk in December/January if the market calms.
